definition: The Hough transform () is a feature extraction technique used in image analysis, computer vision, pattern recognition, and digital image processing.
details: The purpose of the technique is to find imperfect instances of objects within a certain class of shapes by a voting procedure. This voting procedure is carried out in a parameter space, from which object candidates are obtained as local maxima in a so-called accumulator space that is explicitly constructed by the algorithm for computing the Hough transform. Mathematically it is simply the Radon transform in the plane, known since at least 1917, but the Hough transform refers to its use in image analysis. The classical Hough transform was concerned with the identification of lines in the image, but later the Hough transform has been extended to identifying positions of arbitrary shapes, most commonly circles or ellipses. The Hough transform as it is universally used today was invented by Richard Duda and Peter Hart in 1972, who called it a "generalized Hough transform" after the related 1962 patent of Paul Hough. The transform was popularized in the computer vision community by Dana H. Ballard through a 1981 journal article titled "Generalizing the Hough transform to detect arbitrary shapes".

explainer.lead: The Hough transform is a feature extraction technique used in image analysis, computer vision, pattern recognition, and digital image processing. It matters because it finds imperfect instances of shapes through a voting procedure.

tiers.eli5: Every edge point votes for the lines or shapes that could pass through it, and whatever gets the most votes wins.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run the voting in a parameter space and take local maxima in an accumulator space as object candidates, originally for lines and later for circles and ellipses. A pitfall is that noisy or dense scenes can produce spurious peaks.
tiers.paperLevel: Mathematically it is the Radon transform in the plane, known since at least 1917; the transform maps points into a parameter space where candidates are local maxima in an explicitly constructed accumulator space. It handles imperfect instances rather than exact shapes.

explainer.example: Detect a line by letting each edge pixel vote for candidate lines in parameter space, then reading the strongest peak in the accumulator as the line.
